<?php

class Fibonacci
{
    private int $mod;
    private array $calculatedNumbers;

    public function __construct(int $mod)
    {
        $this->calculatedNumbers = [
            0 => 1,
            1 => 1
        ];
        $this->mod = $mod;
    }

    public function fib(int $n): int
    {
        if (array_key_exists($n, $this->calculatedNumbers)) {
            return $this->calculatedNumbers[$n];
        }

        $k = intdiv($n, 2);

        if ($n % 2 === 0) {
            $res = (
                $this->fib($k) * $this->fib($k) +
                $this->fib($k - 1) * $this->fib($k - 1)
            ) % $this->mod;
        } else {
            $res = (
                $this->fib($k) * $this->fib($k + 1) +
                $this->fib($k - 1) * $this->fib($k)
            ) % $this->mod;
        }

        $this->calculatedNumbers[$n] = $res;
        return $res;
    }
}

class Exponentation
{
    public static function calc(int $a, int $b, int $m): int
    {
        if ($b === 0) {
            return 1;
        }

        if ($b === 1) {
            return $a;
        }

        if ($b % 2 === 0) {
            return self::calc(($a * $a) % $m, intdiv($b, 2), $m);
        }

        return ($a * self::calc(
            ($a * $a) % $m,
            intdiv($b - 1, 2),
            $m
        )) % $m;
    }
}

class Solver
{
    private int $n;
    private int $k;
    private int $l;
    private int $mod;

    private function read(InputReader $in): void
    {
        $this->n = $in->nextLong();
        $this->k = $in->nextLong();
        $this->l = $in->nextLong();
        $this->mod = $in->nextLong();
    }

    public function solve(InputReader $in): void
    {
        $this->read($in);

        if ($this->l !== 64 && (1 << $this->l) - 1 < $this->k) {
            echo "0\n";
            return;
        }

        $zeroPos = (new Fibonacci($this->mod))->fib($this->n + 1);
        $onePos = Exponentation::calc(2, $this->n, $this->mod) - $zeroPos;

        while ($onePos < 0) {
            $onePos += $this->mod;
        }

        $res = 1;

        for ($i = 0; $i < $this->l; $i++) {
            if (($this->k & (1 << $i)) !== 0) {
                $res *= $onePos;
            } else {
                $res *= $zeroPos;
            }

            $res %= $this->mod;
        }

        echo ($res % $this->mod) . "\n";
    }
}

class InputReader
{
    private array $tokens;
    private int $index = 0;

    public function __construct()
    {
        $input = trim(stream_get_contents(STDIN));
        $this->tokens = $input === ''
            ? []
            : preg_split('/\s+/', $input);
    }

    public function next(): string
    {
        return $this->tokens[$this->index++];
    }

    public function nextInt(): int
    {
        return (int)$this->next();
    }

    public function nextLong(): int
    {
        return (int)$this->next();
    }
}

$in = new InputReader();
(new Solver())->solve($in);

source_data.prob_desc_description: We all know that GukiZ often plays with arrays. Now he is thinking about this problem: how many arrays a, of length n, with non-negative elements strictly less then 2l meet the following condition: ? Here operation  means bitwise AND (in Pascal it is equivalent to and, in C/C++/Java/Python it is equivalent to &), operation  means bitwise OR (in Pascal it is equivalent to , in C/C++/Java/Python it is equivalent to |). Because the answer can be quite large, calculate it modulo m. This time GukiZ hasn't come up with solution, and needs you to help him!
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: In the single line print the number of arrays satisfying the condition above modulo m.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: First and the only line of input contains four integers n, k, l, m (2 ≤ n ≤ 1018, 0 ≤ k ≤ 1018, 0 ≤ l ≤ 64, 1 ≤ m ≤ 109 + 7).
source_data.prob_desc_notes: NoteIn the first sample, satisfying arrays are {1, 1}, {3, 1}, {1, 3}.In the second sample, only satisfying array is {1, 1}.In the third sample, satisfying arrays are {0, 3, 3}, {1, 3, 2}, {1, 3, 3}, {2, 3, 1}, {2, 3, 3}, {3, 3, 0}, {3, 3, 1}, {3, 3, 2}, {3, 3, 3}.
